genre_interactions.mechanism: argument reaches verdicts without evidence while forensics accumulates evidence without verdicts, and the juxtaposition prevents either mode from becoming the series' authority on truth
genre_interactions.risk: the contrast can look like the series refusing to commit to any method of knowing

genre_interactions.mechanism: a contested transmission needs positions that can be voiced at length without adjudication, so the argument mode supplies the legitimacy debate that succession cannot conduct procedurally
genre_interactions.risk: succession conflict can drift into talk and lose the pressure of an office that must actually be filled

genre_interactions.mechanism: public contest for an office against private grief over what a family owes and is owed, with the same people required to act in both registers at once
genre_interactions.risk: the two scales can cancel each other's weight, leaving neither the office nor the household sufficiently costly

genre_interactions.mechanism: a contested transmission makes the merit record actionable, because holders must justify standing before they can claim and the archive becomes the arena rather than the background
genre_interactions.risk: the archive can be reduced to a weapon in a succession fight and lose its independent interest as a truth-relation

genre_interactions.mechanism: late in the horizon the institution's own history becomes an object of institutional process, so the meta mode stops being commentary and becomes procedure with a cost
genre_interactions.risk: the convergence can feel like the series examining itself instead of its question

genre_interactions.mechanism: framing history as written resists the saga's illusion of unmediated continuity, so the reader cannot simply inherit a generation's perspective without noticing the framing
genre_interactions.risk: continuous framing reminders can dull investment in every generation and make the horizon feel like an exercise

genre_interactions.mechanism: civic drama needs decisions under pressure while argument drama wants pressure suspended for scrutiny, and the clash is productive because each exposes what the other suppresses
genre_interactions.risk: units can stall between deciding and deliberating, satisfying neither mode

genre_interactions.mechanism: household scale forces positions to be voiced by people who must live together afterwards, limiting rhetorical freedom and making every argument carry a future

open_questions: Genre face: no genre is named in the vision. Should archival-institutional drama be the series' public frame, or should the generational saga or the forensic mode be what a reader is promised first? This decides pacing expectations and what a single Book is permitted to be.

Nature of the founding fraud: was the founding hero a fraud as a person, or was a true person buried under a fabricated account? The architecture proposes gradual accretion of claims as a working default, but the answer fixes what evidence can mean for seventy Books.

Reader knowledge ceiling: may the reader ever hold the complete truth while the characters do not, or must the reader's knowledge stay permanently partial? A complete-for-the-reader design makes the series about consequences; a permanently partial design makes it about the conditions of knowing.

Whether the series may spend a Book on honest demolition: is destruction of one or more institutions permitted mid-horizon, with several Books living in the honest absence, or must every institution survive the whole series?

Whether an honest act may be reversed by a later generation: does the architecture allow backsliding, or is the accumulation of honesty monotonic? Backsliding makes the cost of honesty feel real; monotonicity protects the optimism.

Cost currency weighting: should the goods honesty spends be primarily material - safety, provision, order - or primarily dignitary - recognition, standing, meaning? The architecture proposes material-early and dignitary-late; the reverse would produce a colder and more abstract series.

Institutional focus: are all three institutions equally load-bearing, or is one of them the protagonist institution for the horizon? The architecture treats them as co-present while proposing the archive as correctable and the office as least repairable.

Ending form: is there a single terminal settlement for the whole series, or a set of parallel settlements across generations that the last phase selects among? Chosen rather than exhausted can be satisfied either way, but not by the same final unit.

Audience and density: is this a literary readership tolerant of seventy volumes of procedure, or a broad readership needing a stronger recurring through-line? The proposed aesthetic of restraint, inventory and procedural surface is expensive to read.

Whether any figure may recur across generations as a continuous presence: the architecture assumes not, because mortality is an engine, but a small number of long-lived or extensively documented figures would change what the reader can be shown.

Chronological contract: does the series commit to forward chronology, or may a unit move backward to a generation that could not have known? The architecture assumes forward chronology with gaps; retrospection would let the series show a lie being constructed, which it currently cannot.
Moral address: is the reader ever invited to judge a generation, or is sympathy maintained with every position? This decides whether the series' honesty functions as a mirror or as a verdict.

opportunities.title: Publication order as the reader's evidentiary sequence
opportunities.description: The architecture already gives the reader a knowledge position no character can occupy. A stronger version would treat the series' own reading order as a fourth archival sequence: fragments arrive in an order that no generation ever experienced, so a reader who reaches a late phase holds a combination that never existed in the fiction. This would let the horizon's length do evidentiary work rather than merely accumulate cost, and it would make rereading a genuinely different reading rather than a memory exercise.
opportunities.artistic_potential: Turns the seventy-Book form into an epistemic instrument and gives the series a way to make its own length meaningful for the central question rather than merely necessary for its cost economy.
opportunities.faithfulness_to_author_intent: High. The vision already withholds completion and asks the question to stay open; an order-dependent reader position sharpens that without contradicting anything stated.

opportunities.title: A generation that dismantles honestly and lives in the absence
opportunities.description: The vision asks whether the institution is worth keeping once it is honest, which implies keeping is a genuine option but not an inevitable one. A branch in which one generation dismantles an institution honestly - paying the full cost, naming what is lost, refusing to replace it with a new founding story - and several subsequent units live inside the honest absence would test the premise rather than illustrate it. It would let the series demonstrate what its own optimism is worth when the object of hope is gone.
opportunities.artistic_potential: Very high. It supplies the strongest available test of the vision's question and would make the terminal choice feel like a choice rather than an inheritance of the same option. It also protects against the series becoming an argument for conservation by default.
opportunities.faithfulness_to_author_intent: Moderate to high but not assumed. The vision is optimistic and explicitly refuses to declare the argument over; demolition with an honest aftermath is one reading of that, but a reader could reasonably experience it as the series becoming a different, darker project than the one described.
